title: Language Models Change Facts Based on the Way You Talk

bias_targets.methodology: Prepending real conversational histories (sociolinguistic prefixes) from users of different racial and ethnic backgrounds to objective questions across various domains to measure response variance using generalized linear mixed models.
Prepending real conversational histories from male, female, and non-binary users to objective questions to measure response variance using generalized linear mixed models.
Prepending real conversational histories from users of different age groups to objective questions to measure response variance using generalized linear mixed models.
Prepending real conversational histories from users of different religious affiliations to objective questions to measure response variance using generalized linear mixed models.

Prepending real conversational histories from users of different birth regions and current regions of residence to objective questions to measure response variance using generalized linear mixed models.
Prepending real conversational histories from users with different levels of education to objective questions to measure response variance using generalized linear mixed models.

Prepending real conversational histories from users with different employment statuses (e.g., working, unemployed, retired) to objective questions to measure response variance using generalized linear mixed models.
